figures.title: Chapter map
figures.why: the chapter is one function x(t): the map shows the single spine the parts hang off
figures.data: the part structure of the chapter (Part 0-14)
figures.read: every tool in this chapter is the slope or the area of one function

figures.title: The four sign quadrants of motion
figures.why: negative is a label on a chosen axis, not a statement about speeding up
figures.data: the four sign combinations of velocity and acceleration
figures.read: same signs of v and a mean speeding up; opposite signs mean slowing down

figures.title: Area under the v-t graph is displacement
figures.why: the area picture is the graphs-as-calculators toolkit; the sign of the area is a trap
figures.data: v(t) = 10 - 5t m/s on t in [0,4], crossing zero at t = 2 s
figures.read: net displacement is the signed total; distance is the unsigned total

figures.title: Free-fall v-t graph for an upward throw
figures.why: one line of slope -g holds the whole throw: peak, symmetry, return speed
figures.read: slope -g throughout; zero crossing is the peak; return speed -v0 at 2v0/g

figures.title: Phase-space ellipse for a = -kx
figures.why: the v-x loop shows boundedness and turning points at a glance
figures.data: v^2 = v0^2 - k x^2 with v0 = 4, k = 4 (upper half, x in [-2,2])
figures.read: turning points at x = ± v0/sqrt(k) where v = 0; speed peaks at v0 at x = 0

figures.title: Triage — route by what is given
figures.why: the triage list is a decision tree; the flowchart makes the first question visible
figures.read: the first question names the tool; the rest is execution

drawings.title: Position vs displacement vs distance
drawings.show: a number line ($x$-axis) with a particle starting at $x=2$, moving to $x=5$, then back to $x=3$. The displacement from start to finish is $+1$ (from 2 to 3). The total distance is $3+2=5$ (2→5 is 3, 5→3 is 2). Labels: "displacement = 1 m", "distance = 5 m".
drawings.search: "displacement vs distance one dimension number line diagram"

drawings.title: Instantaneous velocity as the tangent slope
drawings.show: an $x$–$t$ graph with a curve; at time $t_0$, a tangent line drawn to the curve; the slope of the tangent labelled as $v(t_0)=dx/dt$; the chord between $t_0$ and $t_0+\Delta t$ shown for comparison, with its slope labelled as $\bar{v}$.
drawings.search: "instantaneous velocity tangent slope x-t graph diagram"

drawings.title: Acceleration and the three graphs
drawings.show: three stacked graphs sharing the same time axis. Top: $x$–$t$ (a parabola for constant positive $a$). Middle: $v$–$t$ (a straight line with positive slope). Bottom: $a$–$t$ (a horizontal line above the axis). Annotations: "slope of $x$–$t$ = $v$", "slope of $v$–$t$ = $a$", "area under $v$–$t$ = $\Delta x$".
drawings.search: "x-t v-t a-t graphs constant acceleration stacked diagram"

drawings.title: Deriving the equations from the $v$–$t$ graph
drawings.show: a $v$–$t$ graph with a straight line from $(0,u)$ to $(t,v)$ with slope $a$. The area under the line (a trapezoid) is labelled $s=\frac{(u+v)}{2}t$. The height of the line at $t$ is $v=u+at$. The area of the triangle on top of the rectangle is $\frac{1}{2}at^2$.
drawings.search: "constant acceleration v-t graph area trapezoid derivation diagram"

drawings.title: The $v\,dv/dx$ method
drawings.show: the chain rule $a=dv/dt=(dv/dx)(dx/dt)=v\,dv/dx$ written step-by-step; then the integral $\int v\,dv=\int a(x)\,dx$ shown; the result $v^2/2=\int a(x)\,dx+C$ boxed.
drawings.search: "v dv/dx method variable acceleration chain rule diagram"

drawings.title: Relative velocity in 1-D
drawings.show: two particles $A$ and $B$ on a number line, $A$ at $x_A$ and $B$ at $x_B$ with $x_A>x_B$. $v_A=5$ m/s (rightward), $v_B=3$ m/s (rightward). $v_{AB}=5-3=2$ m/s — $A$ is pulling away from $B$ at 2 m/s. The separation $x_A-x_B$ is increasing.
drawings.search: "relative velocity one dimension two particles diagram"

drawings.title: Piecewise kinematics on a $v$–$t$ graph
drawings.show: a $v$–$t$ graph with three segments: (1) a straight line with positive slope (acceleration phase); (2) a horizontal line (constant velocity); (3) a straight line with negative slope (braking phase). Each segment labelled with its duration and acceleration. The total displacement is the total area under the graph.
drawings.search: "piecewise kinematics v-t graph acceleration constant velocity braking diagram"

drawings.title: The $n$th-second distance
drawings.show: a $v$–$t$ graph for constant positive acceleration with velocity remaining non-negative. Shade the area from $t=n-1$ to $t=n$; it is the signed displacement $\Delta x_n=u+\frac{a}{2}(2n-1)$ in that one-second interval, and equals distance here because velocity does not reverse.
drawings.search: "nth second distance v-t graph constant acceleration shaded area"

drawings.title: Relative velocity: two particles approaching
drawings.show: $A$ is to the left of $B$ ($x_A<x_B$). $A$ moves right at speed $v_A$ and $B$ moves left at speed $v_B$. The positive separation $d=x_B-x_A$ decreases; the relative velocity of $A$ with respect to $B$ is $v_{AB}=v_A-(-v_B)=v_A+v_B$, the closing speed.
drawings.search: "relative velocity two particles approaching closing speed diagram"
